newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends slightly down in wary mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends slightly down in wary mood.

text.p: The Shanghai B share index ended slightly down on Thursday with a wary mood prevailing due to concerns about a possible new crackdown on market volatility, brokers said.

Official newspaper have repeatedly warned over the past week about the risks of stock investment but A shares continued rise until the Thursday afternoon session due to an inflow of speculative hot money.
The B index edged down 0.225 points or 0.31 percent to 73.102 on volume of 21.6 million shares worth $12.1 million.
The A index fell 5.225 points or 0.39 percent to 1,344.302 on heavy turnover of 12.98 billion yuan.

"Domestic unwinding selling emerged in line with falls on the A share market, which pushed the index down," one broker said. "But the downward potential is limited because B shares have not risen as sharply as A shares over the past few weeks."
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded, with 20 down, eight flat and 13 up.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping $0.020 or 9.52 percent to $0.190 on volume of 48,000 shares.

Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products traded the most actively with institutional investors' mixed over its annual report published on Thursday, falling $0.004 or 0.52 percent to $0.754 on volume of 3.5 million shares.

The Shanghai A share index erased its morning gains in the afternoon session on investors jitters over a possible crackdown, brokers said. The SSE30 index fell 24.318 points or 0.68 percent to 3,536.098 points.
Xinjiang Zhonghe was the biggest loser on lower-than-expected earnings, plunging 1.80 yuan or 10.00 percent to 16.20 yuan on volume of 548,100 shares.
